REPORT
Date July 30, /31
Subject (in full) D. A. Rushton alias D. A. Berkeley - Rushton
Made by D. S. I. Duncan. Forwarded by
Sir,
Enquiries show that D. A. Rushton alias D. A. Berkeley -
Rushton arrived in Shanghai from Hongkong on April 7, 1931.
He first resided at No. 17 Yuen Ming Yuen Road where he
registered himself as a British subject and being in Civil
Service. On May 6 he removed to No. 32 Jinkee Road and a
few days later to No. 142 Szechuen Road. In each case he
left without paying for his board and lodgings. He now
resides at No. 311 Route Tenant de la Tour but has made
arrangements to move No. 3-4 Weihaiwei Road in a few days.
Rushton has contracted numerous debts at different
places around town and will in all likelihood be brought
into court as he has so far made no effort to pay up.
In one instance he obtained credit by making a statement
to the effect that he held a position with the Asia
Realty Co., So far I have been unable to ascertain if he
has ever used Brig-Gen Macnaghten's name to enable him
to raise money although the attached letter addressed
to Mrs. Botsford indicates that he is quite capable of
doing so.
Rushton and Ogilvie who is mentioned in the letter,
arrived together from Hongkong.
Rushton is reported to come of a good family and his
parents are said to reside in Singapore. He now styles
himself - D. A. Berkeley - Rushton, manufacturers repre-
sentative.
Anything further of interest learned regarding this
person will be duly reported.
（批：CDM sent the warning for Rush ton 21/7）
J. Le [签名]
Officer i/c Special Branch.
D. S. I.

Yuen Hing Yuen Road
27 - 7 - 37

I am very surprised to receive your
letter yesterday — and have not as yet the details
contained therein.

In the first place it may please you to know that
I have made the necessary arrangements with Arthur Johnson
my cousin, to settle that due charge of Opinions — in
respect of the China Interest. So I am positive you may
rest assured about that. I'm sorry Opinions let
me down.

Also, I haven't seen Art for days - but I
understand from fellows that he has been very busy
lately.

Now, Lady Betty, I wish you could have
conveyed something to me before seizing my Business
Clothes. What is the real reason? - won't you tell
please tell me ? Because if you can only meet me
on common ground - and we talk this matter out, it
would be far better. Furthermore, in spite of the fact that
you may think I've been slack — though I have to
dine with General McNaughten (No 1 of the B.A.T) and
Burger of the same Coy. Now won't you please help
me out for tonight ? And you can have it back tomorrow
if you wish - and we can talk the matter over. Yours sincerely
